q: Mutual funds in India are constituted as:
e: Mutual funds in India are set up as Trusts under the Indian Trusts Act, 1882. Unitholders are the beneficiaries of the trust.

q: Mutual funds are constituted as Trusts in India. Who are the beneficiaries of the trust?
e: Unitholders are the beneficial owners of the trust property. The trustees hold the property in trust for the unitholders.

q: The minimum net worth required for an Asset Management Company (AMC) is:
e: SEBI mandates a minimum net worth of ₹50 crore for AMCs at all times.

q: The sponsor of a mutual fund must contribute at least __ to the net worth of the AMC.
e: The sponsor must contribute a minimum of 40% to the net worth of the AMC.

q: A sponsor must have a sound track record in financial services for at least:
e: Sponsors must have a minimum 5-year track record in financial services and demonstrated financial soundness.

q: What proportion of the Board of Trustees must be independent?
e: At least 2/3rd of the trustees must be independent — not associated with the sponsor.

q: The role of the Custodian in a mutual fund is to:
o: Hold the securities of the scheme in safe custody
e: The custodian holds securities and other assets of the scheme in safe custody. They are SEBI-registered and independent of the AMC.

q: Registrar and Transfer Agents (RTA) primarily handle:
o: Investor records, transactions, and unit allotment
e: RTAs maintain investor records, process applications, allot units, handle redemptions, and dispatch account statements.

q: Who appoints the Asset Management Company (AMC)?
e: Trustees appoint the AMC, with prior approval from SEBI. AMC operates under the trust deed and IMA (Investment Management Agreement).

q: AMFI is best described as:
o: An industry body of mutual funds
e: AMFI (Association of Mutual Funds in India) is the industry body — not a regulator. SEBI is the statutory regulator.

q: Which of the following is NOT a function of the Trustees?
o: Ensuring AMC compliance with SEBI regulations
e: Trustees oversee — they do NOT make investment decisions. The AMC handles day-to-day fund management.

q: Mutual funds in India are regulated primarily by:
e: SEBI is the primary regulator under SEBI (Mutual Funds) Regulations, 1996.

q: Beneficiaries of a mutual fund trust:
e: Unitholders are the beneficiaries.

q: Sponsor must contribute __ to AMC net worth:
e: Minimum 40%.

q: Minimum AMC net worth required:
e: ₹50 crore.

q: Trustees must include __ independent members:
e: 2/3rd minimum.

q: Custodian role:
e: Holds securities/assets in safe custody.

q: The Investment Management Agreement (IMA) is signed between:
e: IMA is signed between Trustees and AMC, governing the AMC's management of mutual fund schemes.

q: A change in the sponsor of a mutual fund requires:
o: Prior approval of SEBI and a no-load exit window
e: Change of sponsor or controlling interest requires SEBI prior approval AND a no-load exit window for unitholders to exit if they wish.

q: AMC's minimum net worth requirement of ₹50 crore must be:
o: Met only at the time of registration
Met only when AUM exceeds ₹500 cr
e: AMC must maintain minimum net worth of ₹50 crore at all times — not just at registration.

q: The Investment Management Agreement (IMA) is between:
e: IMA is signed between the Trustees and the AMC, governing the AMC's management of the schemes.

q: Whose role is it to track corporate actions like bonus, dividend, or rights issues in companies where the mutual fund scheme has invested?
e: The Custodian tracks and processes corporate actions on the securities held in safe custody — including bonus, dividends, rights issues, and other entitlements.

q: Investment of funds pooled from unitholders is the responsibility of:
e: The AMC is responsible for managing the investments of the scheme. Trustees oversee, Custodian holds securities, RTA handles investor records.

q: The Sponsor of a mutual fund is responsible or liable for losses to the scheme:
o: Up to the initial contribution made towards setting up the mutual fund
e: The sponsor's liability is LIMITED to the initial contribution made towards setting up the mutual fund. This is part of the standard risk factors disclosed.

q: AMFI is responsible for which of the following?
o: Conducting the NISM V-A certification examination
Issuing ARN to certified distributors and maintaining industry data
e: AMFI issues ARN, maintains industry data, runs investor awareness, sets best practices. NISM (separate body) conducts certification. SEBI approves/regulates schemes.

q: The Trust Deed of a mutual fund is executed between:
e: Trust Deed is between Sponsor (settlor) and Trustees. SEBI prescribes mandatory clauses. Trust Deed governs the trust's operation.

q: The Investment Management Agreement (IMA) governs:
o: Relationship between Trustees and AMC for managing schemes
e: IMA between Trustees and AMC defines how the AMC manages the schemes — investment authority, fees, reporting obligations.

q: The minimum number of independent directors on the Board of Directors of an AMC is:
e: At least 50% of AMC's Board of Directors must be independent — not associated with the sponsor or any entity in the same group.

q: A Custodian must be __ from the Sponsor and AMC:
e: Custodian must be SEBI-registered AND independent of the Sponsor/AMC to avoid conflict of interest. Holds securities of the scheme on behalf of unitholders.

q: The Auditor of a mutual fund scheme is appointed by:
e: Trustees appoint the auditor of the schemes. The auditor must be different from the auditor of the AMC. This is a key check on the AMC.

q: A Registrar and Transfer Agent (RTA) handles:
o: Investor records, allotment, redemption, account statements, dividend processing
e: RTAs are SEBI-registered intermediaries that handle the entire investor-facing operational backbone — folio creation, transactions, statements, payouts.

q: A change in controlling interest of the sponsor of a mutual fund requires:
o: Prior SEBI approval AND no-load exit window for unitholders
e: Change of sponsor / controlling interest is a material change. Requires SEBI prior approval AND a 30-day no-load exit window for investors who want to exit.

q: The Compliance Officer of an AMC is responsible for:
o: Ensuring AMC complies with SEBI regulations and code of conduct
e: Compliance Officer ensures regulatory compliance, signs the due diligence certificate for NFOs, and acts as the bridge to SEBI on regulatory matters.

q: An AMC of a mutual fund:
o: Can be the Trustee of the same fund
Cannot be the Trustee — separation of roles required
e: AMC and Trustees must be SEPARATE entities — checks-and-balances structure. AMC is a SEBI-registered company appointed by Trustees.

q: CRISIL and ICRA are SEBI-approved as:
o: Valuation agencies for debt securities used in mutual funds
e: CRISIL and ICRA are the SEBI-approved valuation agencies for debt securities. Their valuations feed into NAV computation for debt holdings.

q: A "Trustee Company" — its Board of Directors must have at least __ independent directors:
e: For Trustee Company, at least 2/3rd of directors must be independent. Stricter than AMC (50%) — given trustees' fiduciary role to unitholders.

q: The sponsor of a mutual fund must demonstrate:
o: Sound track record of at least 5 years in financial services + financial soundness
e: Sponsor must have minimum 5-year track record in financial services AND demonstrate financial soundness. SEBI verifies these before granting registration.

q: The Compliance Officer of an AMC signs:
o: The Due Diligence Certificate filed with SEBI for NFO
e: Compliance Officer signs the Due Diligence Certificate confirming regulatory compliance and disclosure adequacy. Filed along with the draft offer document.

q: The two SEBI-approved debt valuation agencies are:
e: CRISIL and ICRA are the SEBI-approved valuation agencies for debt securities. Their valuations feed into mutual fund NAV.

q: The role of a Mutual Fund Trustee is best described as:
o: Overseeing the AMC and protecting unitholder interests; ensuring compliance with SEBI regulations
e: Trustees are fiduciaries to unitholders. They oversee the AMC, ensure regulatory compliance, approve scheme launches, but DO NOT make investment decisions (AMC does).

q: An AMC must maintain minimum net worth of:
e: Minimum net worth requirement: ₹50 crore at all times — not just at registration.

q: Custodian's primary role is:
o: Holding scheme's securities in safe custody, processing corporate actions
e: Custodian holds securities in safe custody, processes corporate actions (bonus, dividends, rights), and is independent of AMC/Sponsor.

q: AMFI is:
o: The industry association of mutual fund AMCs (issues ARN, runs awareness, sets best practices)
e: AMFI = industry association of AMCs. NOT a regulator (SEBI is). Issues ARN, runs awareness campaigns ("Mutual Funds Sahi Hai"), promotes best practices.
